text:
Morgan: heads up — provisioner queue spiked in us-west1 around 13:02 UTC, attaching notes. seems tied to background-deleter ratecap hitting NVMe iops ceiling.

Sam: seen it too, GPU attach delays ~3-4m, some jobs OOMing because ephemeral dir filled.

Morgan: exact symptom: provisioner waits on attach, root cause looks like lots of small deletes (janitor) causing write amplification + read stalls. iostat snapshot:```Device rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm %utilnvme0n1 0.00 0.00 5.30 320.10 10.2 4096.8 12.9 3.4 1.01 99.3```

Priya: who owns the background deleter config? last change was the rate cap PR we merged last week. maybe it throttled too low under churn.

Carlos: that PR lowered concurrent deletes to 8 to reduce burst IO for pageserver, but with scratch churn and many small files it serializes and causes meta-ops to pile.

Sam: thinking we should temporarily bump concurrency to 32 for us-west1 and fall back after backlog drains. change is in host-cleaner config:```concurrency: 8
burst_limit: 200ms```

infra-bot: rollback window opened for host-cleaner config in us-west1. change-id: hc-ratecap-2026-03-20.

Priya: can we also add a quick healthcheck to fail fast on stale tempfiles (age>10m) instead of relying purely on ratecap? it's cheap and would reduce metadata ops.

Sam: +1. For immediate mitigation i'm going to patch concurrency and increase burst_limit to 800ms. will monitor queue length and %util.

Morgan: @oncall-ops i'll defer to you for the runtime change, but please keep an eye on GPU attach latency and evict logs. also add a short note to incidents if this crosses 5m provisioning delay. :eyes:

oncall-ops: applying patch now to us-west1 host-cleaner (canary 10%). will ramp to 100% in 5m if no regressions.

infra-bot: canary applied to 10% hosts in us-west1.

Sam: canary looks ok so far, %util dropped from ~99 to ~45 on canary. queued attaches on canary hosts cleared.

Priya: opened a follow-up issue to add age-based fast-delete and an adaptive ratecap (based on avg queue depth + nvme util). linking to doc in #eng-infra later.

Carlos: long term we should consider coalescing small deletes into batched ops to reduce metadata churn. adding to roadmap.

Morgan: thanks all. keeping this thread open for post-mortem items.

Sam: post-mortem seeds: immediate mitigation (ratecap bump), medium (age-based fast-delete), long (delete coalescing + heuristics), monitoring (per-host delete latency, nvme util alarm).

infra-bot: incident closed: mitigation successful. incident id: inc-20260320-01.
